options: Jinja — a general-purpose templating language, not syntax dbt invented specifically
Proprietary dbt keywords with no relation to any other language
SQL functions that run inside the warehouse itself
Python functions that must be imported separately into every model
questions.explain: dbt SQL is built on Jinja, a general-purpose templating language — ref(), config(), and is_incremental() are all ordinary Jinja constructs, not warehouse SQL and not dbt-specific syntax.

questions.q: What is the difference between `{{ }}` and `{% %}`?
options: {{ }} is an expression that renders to a value; {% %} is a statement for control flow that renders to nothing itself
They are interchangeable and produce identical output
{{ }} is only valid in YAML files, {% %} only in SQL files
{% %} always produces a table reference
questions.explain: {{ }} produces a value dropped into the SQL (like a ref() call); {% %} controls flow (if/for/set) and doesn't itself render to a value.

questions.q: What does `loop.last` do inside a Jinja `{% for %}` loop?
options: Indicates whether the current iteration is the final one in the loop — useful for skipping a trailing comma
Stops the loop from executing entirely
Reverses the order of the loop's items
Is a function unrelated to Jinja's for loop
questions.explain: loop.last is true only on the final iteration, which is exactly what's needed to add commas between generated items without a trailing comma at the end.

questions.q: Why does dbt SQL use Jinja loops to generate columns like one `sum(case when...)` per status?
options: Because SQL has no loops or variables of its own, so repetitive patterns either get typed by hand or generated once with a small loop
Because the warehouse requires Jinja syntax to execute case statements
Because loops make queries run faster at execution time
Because dbt cannot compile plain case statements without Jinja
questions.explain: Plain SQL has no loop construct; Jinja's for loop is a code-generation tool that writes out repetitive SQL once instead of by hand for each value.

questions.q: Where can you see the actual SQL dbt sends to the warehouse, with all Jinja rendered away?
options: In target/compiled/, or live in dbt Cloud's Compiled Code tab
It cannot be viewed anywhere — Jinja rendering is a black box
Only by contacting dbt Labs support
In the seeds/ folder
questions.explain: Every run writes the fully rendered SQL to target/compiled/, and dbt Cloud's Studio IDE shows the same rendered SQL live in its Compiled Code tab.
